entries.notes: G-6 remains partial: GTI STEP Demo provides MW-scale sCO2 demonstration data (Phase 1: 4 MWe at 500°C; Phase 2 target: 10 MWe at 715°C RCBC). The 50% cycle efficiency target has not yet been demonstrated — it is the Phase 2 goal. Phase 2 data was not available at time of search (October 2024 milestone only covers Phase 1). The fusion-coupling context of G-6 (800-1200K working temperature) is not addressed by STEP Demo (non-fusion, fossil/renewable heat source). The gap is partially closed: intermediate-scale (MW) sCO2 demonstration data now exists showing commercial scalability, but the specific 50% efficiency at fusion-relevant temperatures remains undemonstrated.

candidates.title: Overview of the Helios Design: A Practical Planar Coil Stellarator Fusion Power Plant (Thea Energy, 2025)
candidates.triage: highly relevant — contains quantitative stellarator FPP component lifetime data: first wall 15 FPY (V-4Cr-4Ti vanadium alloy), <7.5 FPY for RAFM steels, coil lifetime 40 years, planned maintenance 84 days every 2 years (88% capacity factor)
candidates.notes: Preconceptual design for Helios (Thea Energy). Planar coil QA stellarator, different topology from HESTIA, but provides stellarator-specific analogue data for blanket/first wall replacement intervals and coil lifetime under neutron irradiation. Uses EUROFER97 structural material (not high-Mn austenitic steel like HESTIA), but neutron damage thresholds and maintenance cadence are directly applicable as analogue estimates.

entries.notes: G-11 addressed with stellarator analogue data from Helios FPP design. Key data: first wall lifetime 15 FPY (vanadium alloy) vs <7.5 FPY (RAFM steel); HTS coil lifetime 40+ years (full plant life) with 1.2m neutron shielding; planned outage 84 days every 2 years yielding 88% capacity factor. HESTIA uses high-Mn austenitic steel (not V44 or EUROFER97) and a different coil geometry — these analogue figures should be used with explicit material-difference caveats. The 88% capacity factor from biennial maintenance is consistent with HESTIA's >80-85% availability target.
